from prometheus_client import CollectorRegistry, Gauge, push_to_gateway

@router.post("/metrics/push/jobs/{job_id}")
async def push_batch_metrics(
    job_id: str,
    payload: MetricPushPayload,
    current_user: User = Depends(get_current_user)
):
    registry = CollectorRegistry()
    gauge = Gauge('batch_job_duration_seconds', 'Runtime of batch job', ['tenant', 'job'], registry=registry)
    gauge.labels(tenant=payload.tenant_slug, job=job_id).set(payload.duration)
    push_to_gateway('pushgateway.internal:9091', job=f'job_{job_id}', registry=registry)
    return {"status": "pushed", "job_id": job_id}
diagnosis: The batch job telemetry push proxy receives tenant_slug inside payload and pushes Prometheus gauges to an internal Pushgateway. It does not verify that payload.tenant_slug matches current_user.tenant_slug, allowing an authenticated client to poison or overwrite competitor SLA runtime metrics and job completion statistics.

corrected_code:
from prometheus_client import CollectorRegistry, Gauge, push_to_gateway

@router.post("/metrics/push/jobs/{job_id}")
async def push_batch_metrics(
    job_id: str,
    payload: MetricPushPayload,
    current_user: User = Depends(get_current_user)
):
    if payload.tenant_slug != current_user.tenant_slug and not current_user.is_system_admin:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="Forbidden: unauthorized tenant slug in metric payload")

    registry = CollectorRegistry()
    gauge = Gauge('batch_job_duration_seconds', 'Runtime of batch job', ['tenant', 'job'], registry=registry)
    gauge.labels(tenant=current_user.tenant_slug, job=job_id).set(payload.duration)
    push_to_gateway('pushgateway.internal:9091', job=f'job_{job_id}', registry=registry)
    return {"status": "pushed", "job_id": job_id}
